patient_information: A 41-year-old male yoga teacher from Europe.
chief_complaint: Itchy skin eruptions on both upper thighs for the past week.
history_of_present_illness: Just after his arrival in Australia from a 3-day beach holiday in Thailand, he developed three intensely itchy skin eruptions on both upper thighs that kept him awake at night. He had no fever, cough, or wheeze and was otherwise completely well.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient recently returned from a 10-day trip to northern Australia for a yoga seminar, with a 3-day stopover on a Thai island for a beach holiday. He was probably infected while lying on the beach or performing yoga exercises in the sand.
physical_exam: On both upper thighs, there were three reddish, serpiginous tracks, about 2 mm in width. Inguinal lymph nodes were not enlarged, the chest was clear, and the rest of the examination was unremarkable.
labs_and_diagnostics: No investigations were required as diagnosis is made clinically, supported by exposure history; skin biopsy is not helpful, no reliable serological tests are available, and blood eosinophilia is present in a minority of cases.
differential_diagnosis: Cutaneous larva migrans (CLM) caused by larvae of animal hookworms, Strongyloides stercoralis (larva currens), adult nematodes such as Gnathostoma species and trematodes (Fasciola species), and migratory myiasis caused by parasitic fly larvae.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was prescribed a single-dose treatment of ivermectin (200 µg/kg), and the itchy eruptions settled within a few days of taking the drug.

images.caption: Three track-like skin eruptions on both upper thighs causing intense itching.
